title.narrative: AFCC2/RI-Lake Victoria Environmental Management Project (Burundi and Rwanda)

description.narrative: The development objectives of the Adaptable Program Loan for the Second Phase of the Lake Victoria Environmental Management Project are to: improve the collaborative management of the transboundary natural resources of Lake Victoria Basin (LVB) for the shared benefits of the partner states; and reduce environmental stress in targeted pollution hotspots and selected degraded sub-catchments to improve the livelihoods of communities, who depend on the natural resources of LVB. There are four components to the project. The first component of the project is strengthening institutional capacity for managing shared water and fisheries resources. This component will focus on building the capacity and increasing the effectiveness of the existing national institutions in Burundi and Rwanda to manage the water and fisheries resources in the Kagera River Basin, and improve the cooperative management of shared transboundary natural resources of the Lake Victoria Basin. The second component of the project is point source pollution control and prevention. The main objective of this component is to reduce environmental stresses from point source pollution, especially municipal wastewaters, on the rivers, wetlands, and lakes in the LVB portion of Rwanda and Burundi. The third component of the project is watershed management. This component seeks to reduce environmental stresses in the LVB through integrated watershed management, including the rehabilitation of degraded wetlands and river banks, and the adoption of on-farm soil and water conservation programs on the hillsides. The fourth component of the project is project coordination and management. This component will provide resources necessary for effective project coordination, regional and national levels communication and capacity building, monitoring and evaluation activities, and sharing of information among countries.

The objectives of the Project are to contribute to: (i) the improvement of the collaborative management of the trans-boundary natural resources of the LVB among the Partner States; and (ii) the improvement of environmental management of targeted pollution hotspots and selected degraded sub-catchments for the benefit of communities who depend on the natural resources of LVB.

comment.narrative: Achieved (98%). The target was not amended throughout the project. For Burundi, this indicator also includes the number of children benefiting from access to improved sanitation facilities at education institutions. The percentage of female beneficiaries (36.2% fr Rwanda and 54% for Burundi) was achieved for both countries. The minimum female participation required by law is 30% in both countries.

title.narrative: Number of hectares under sustainable land management practices in the targeted sub-catchments

comment.narrative: Target exceeded (118% achieved). The target was reached by December 2016 (13,150 ha) . Activites included terracing, river bank protection, wetlands protection and reforestation.

title.narrative: Target industries in the LVB adopting Cleaner Production Technologies

comment.narrative: Target significantly exceeded. The original target was measured as a percentage (30% from 25 target industries) to reflect an absolute number 5. Twenty five industries in Rwanda adopted such technologies. Kigali, the capital city, is by far the largest urban center in the Basin, thus providing a much larger number and range of industries which could participate in reducing industrial pollution by promoting on-site pre-treatment of waste from industries and enhanced resource efficiency in the use of raw materials – through sorting, reuse, and recycling activities.

title.narrative: Proportion of farmers in project intervention areas using improved farm methods

comment.narrative: The original target was achieved. However, it was not possible to disaggregate by gender as originally required and a 50% split is assumed. Poor land use and poor farming practices cause soil erosion and lead to siltation of water bodies. This indicator measures the level of adoption of on-farm soil and water conservation programs on the hillsides, as a way to reduce non-point sources of pollution. Good farming practices also improve land productivity and ultimately would also impact farmers' incomes.

title.narrative: Target industries in the LVB adhering to the harmonized effluent standards

comment.narrative: The target was significantly exceeded.The original target was measured as a percentage (25% from 25 target industries) to reflect an absolute number 8. The actual achieved at project end is based on LVBC Results Framework tables, showing that Rwanda achieved 25 (against a target 3) and Burundi achieved 5 (against a target 2). The Project Completion Report from LVBC (dated March 2018), however, reported a much larger number 76 (RW 71, BI 5).

title.narrative: Number of education centers with improved on-site sanitation facilities -Burundi only

comment.narrative: The original target was 100% achieved. Building on an existing study of public sanitation needs in the second largest town, Gitega, the project supported similar analyses in 3 other provincial capitals within target watersheds, and improve sanitation facilities i schools and market places, which posed problems of concentrated sources of sewage and risks to public health.

title.narrative: Number of urban pollution hotspots addressed through investments to control wastewater pollution

comment.narrative: Revised target achieved. The target for Rwanda was reduced to 0 in 2016 because most of the money was reallocated in favor of component 3, while retaining funding for only preparatory studies for a future phase of sanitation investments. In Burundi, the target had to be reduced because of depreciation of the SDR.

title.narrative: Number of urban centers with assessment of point source pollution hotspots (Pollution Control Plans)

comment.narrative: The original target was 100% achieved; overachieved in Burundi (3 against target of 2), and underachieved in Rwanda (5 against a target of 6) In Rwanda, pollution level assessments and Pollution Control Plans were prepared for the districts of Kicukiro, Gasabo, Musanze, Huye, and Muhanga. This indicator measured progress towards the identification of point source pollution hotspots in priority municipalities. Potential point source pollution hotspots were: municipal slaughterhouses, markets, bus stations, soccer field, schools, health clinics, etc.

title.narrative: Number of hectares of degraded wetlands restored and/or rehabilitated by communities in targeted sub-catchments

comment.narrative: The target was reached in 2016, and exceed by over 50% by end project. Rehabilitation of degraded wetlands and river banks and the adoption of on-farm soil and water conservation programs on the hillsides helps reduce environmental stresses and addresses (amongther things) non-point sources of pollution (sediment loads, nutrients, and agrochemicals) in LVB.

title.narrative: Development of National Strategic Plan for Wetland Conservation

comment.narrative: This target was achieved. Both countries have plans developed, and the one for Burundi was approved by government. The one for Rwanda has been validated but not yet approved.

title.narrative: Communication notes, with summary reports on project achievements and progress on indicators, are made avaialble to stakeholders atleast on a quarterly basis

comment.narrative: This indicator was achieved. The actual value at end project was provided by the LVBC, although it is not clear what it reflects, nor does the PAD provide details as to how the target was set. Both countries communicated project news and results through various media. In Burundi, the project supported newsletters and brochure which were regularly produced but did not contain data on result indicators in Burundi. In addition, there were radio broadcasts, the website was maintained, and a mini documentary on LVEMP II achievements was produced. For Rwanda, the webpage was developed (http://lvemp2.rema.gov.rw) and regularly updated, 12 Newsletters (http://lvemp2.rema.gov.rw/news/newsletter/) published; 5 short videos; a Semi-Annual communication report was prepared and submitted; The documentary on LVEMP II achievements was produced, 600 brochures were produced and disseminated. There reports were shared with stakeholders on a regular basis. -

title.narrative: Percent of community natural resource management subprojects whose implementation is rated satisfactory or better in the targeted sub-catchments

comment.narrative: This target was achieved (68 percent in Burundi and 82 percent in Rwanda). The results were based on completion surveys conducted on 34 CDD sub-projects in Burundi, and 54 CDD and 22 CMI projects in Rwanda (source: project completion reports for Burundi and Rwanda).

title.narrative: M&E/MIS system implemented and updated according to schedule

comment.narrative: The revised target was achieved. Originally, this indicator was divided into two indicators, one for the M&E system and another for the MIS (Management Information System) but the two were combined into one since the M&E and MIS systems were combined. According t the PAD, the first reports were to produced in year 4 of the project implementation. In both countries, M&E tools were developed and used to document project achievements on a quarterly basis; GIS data were collected (GPS) for all project activities and were regularly updated.
